title: The Jam
hook_spoken: They put the coin in. And nothing dropped.
hook_frame0: A giant vending machine fills the frame. A glowing violet coin hangs half inside the slot and a snack labelled Your Coaching dangles off its spiral, stuck at the lip. Caption: They put the coin in.
pain: People enquire, then ghost. They were interested, but the path to booking had too many steps (people wasting the coach's time, leads lost between first message and call).
format: Original: stuck vending machine physics gag, then a keypad strip down
story: A lead puts a coin in, the machine jams, we count the seven steps between interested and booked, strip it to three, and the snack drops.

beats.vo: They put the coin in. And nothing dropped.
beats.hero_visual: Full bleed vending machine, snack hanging off the spiral by one corner, violet coin in the slot, red JAM light blinking.
beats.motion: Coin clinks in, spiral turns, snack tips forward, stops on a hard stall with a 3 frame shake. Light blinks.
beats.sound: Coin clink, motor whirr, grinding stall thud (hook hit at frame 0).

beats.vo: Here is why. Between I am interested and booked, most coaches make people take seven steps. Reply. Open a link. Find the form. Name. Email. Pick a time. Confirm.
beats.hero_visual: The whole screen becomes a huge keypad of seven fat buttons, each stamped with a step. A violet finger glow presses them in order.
beats.motion: Each button depresses with a squash and lights up in turn. The row gets slightly harder to press: later buttons are greyer.
beats.sound: Seven rising keypad clicks, each a little lower in volume, last one dull.

beats.vo: Count yours. Every extra step is one more spring that can jam. Cut it to three. A question. A time. Done.
beats.hero_visual: The keypad: four of the seven buttons snap out sideways and fall off the bottom, leaving three giant buttons labelled Question, Time, Done that slide together and lock into a tight row.
beats.motion: Buttons snap off with an elastic ease. The remaining three magnet together with a small overshoot and a light sweep.
beats.sound: Four quick snaps, a magnetic clunk as the three join.

beats.vo: Fewer steps, and the snack drops. Comment STEPS and I'll DM you the three step version we use at DUXIO.
beats.hero_visual: Back to the vending machine wide: spiral turns, snack drops with a bounce into the tray, a door flap swings. Keyword card STEPS slides into the tray window.
beats.motion: Snack falls with two decaying bounces. The keyword card lands with a 3 percent overshoot. Last frame matches frame 0, snack hanging again so it loops.
beats.sound: Spiral whirr, bounce thuds, satisfying tray clack, soft pluck on the keyword.

why_it_stops_scroll: A stuck snack is a universal tiny tragedy. The viewer has to see if it drops, and the payoff is the satisfying snap of buttons.

title: The Gap
hook_spoken: Twenty one days of follow up. Watch where it stops.
hook_frame0: Top down view of a huge snaking line of 21 standing dominoes across the whole frame with a violet marble frozen an inch from the first one. Caption: Watch where it stops.
pain: One message then silence. Coaches follow up once and then the chain dies (the lead gave up, a business that depends on constant availability).
format: Original: domino chain run, then a tighter rebuild
story: A follow up chain falls for three dominoes and dies at a big gap, so we close the gaps and the whole chain tips into a booked call.

beats.vo: Twenty one days of follow up. Watch where it stops.
beats.hero_visual: Full frame top down domino snake, each tile numbered Day 1 to Day 21, marble about to touch Day 1.
beats.motion: Marble rolls in, first tile tips, chain falls fast.
beats.sound: Hook hit, rapid wooden clacks.

beats.vo: Day one. Day two. Day three. And then a gap.
beats.hero_visual: The fall stops dead at Day 3. The camera view is the gap itself: a huge empty stretch of floor with a chunky ruler measuring it, red tick marks.
beats.motion: Last tile leans, does not reach, wobbles back. A ruler draws across the gap and a red number counts up as the days pass.
beats.sound: Clacks stop, one dull thud, ruler ticking.

beats.vo: Most coaches follow up once, then wait two weeks. A chain only falls if every gap is small enough. Keep every gap under a week, and keep each message short.
beats.hero_visual: A reset: tiles zip back up into new spacing on a calendar grid, tight at the start and a little wider later. Week markers run under them.
beats.motion: Tiles spring upright one by one with a pop. Spacing slides in an eased snap to the new layout.
beats.sound: Rapid pop sequence rising in pitch as tiles stand.

beats.vo: Now watch. Every tile falls, and the last one lands right on a booked call. Comment CHAIN and I'll DM you the spacing we use.
beats.hero_visual: Full run again, camera tracks the fall along the S curve, last tile lands on a big calendar card that flips to Booked (Example). Keyword card CHAIN.
beats.motion: Chain falls with a pitch that rises per tile, the last tile pushes the card into a flip. Keyword card lands with overshoot.
beats.sound: Rising wooden clack ladder, a deep satisfying land thud, pluck.

why_it_stops_scroll: Domino runs are hypnotic and the viewer wants to know where it breaks. The rising pitch of the clacks is pure ASMR.

title: Ten Marbles
hook_spoken: Ten people asked about your coaching. How many reach the bottom?
hook_frame0: Ten glowing violet marbles stacked at the neck of a huge glass funnel with three hatches down its side. Caption: 10 asked. How many reach the bottom?
pain: Flying blind on numbers. Coaches do not know how many enquiries answer, book or show up.
format: Original: marble funnel with trapdoor gates, counting game
story: Ten marbles drop through three gates and the viewer sees how few reach the end, then learns the four number sticky note to track.

beats.vo: Ten people asked about your coaching. How many reach the bottom?
beats.hero_visual: Full screen glass funnel, ten marbles ready, three hatch gates labelled Answered, Booked, Showed up.
beats.motion: Marbles hover and tremble, then release.
beats.sound: Hook hit then marble rattle.

beats.vo: Gate one, did you answer them. Gate two, did they book. Gate three, did they show up. Watch.
beats.hero_visual: Close on each gate in turn: a hatch swings open and some marbles drop out into the dark and turn grey while the rest roll on. Example counts: 10, then 6, then 4, then 3.
beats.motion: Hatch flaps down with a snap, grey marbles fall off screen with a bounce, a big number rolls down to the remaining count.
beats.sound: Hatch clunk, marble clatter falling, dull plops, number tick.

beats.vo: Most coaches never count. So here is the cheapest fix there is. A sticky note. Four lines. Asked. Answered. Booked. Showed up. Fill it in every Friday.
beats.hero_visual: A giant yellow sticky note fills the screen and a pen handwrites four lines with blank number boxes, then boxes fill with Example numbers.
beats.motion: Handwriting draws on with a path stroke, boxes count up and land with a small pop. Note peels slightly at one corner.
beats.sound: Pen scratch, tick per number, paper rustle.

beats.vo: The gate that leaks most is the one to fix first. Comment JAR and I'll DM you the note to copy.
beats.hero_visual: The funnel returns, the biggest leaking gate glows red and a patch slides over it, a marble count pours into a full jar. Keyword card JAR.
beats.motion: Red glow pulses once, patch slaps on with a squash, marbles tumble into a jar. Last frame holds marbles at the funnel top for the loop.
beats.sound: Slap, marble pour, pluck.

why_it_stops_scroll: A counting game with physical objects makes the viewer guess an answer before it is shown. Marbles dropping through gates is deeply satisfying.

title: The Block Tower
hook_spoken: Your business is a wobbly tower. Guess which block you are.
hook_frame0: A tall wooden block tower fills the frame, wobbling slightly, with the bottom block labelled YOU in big letters. A single block in the middle is slid half out. Caption: Pull the wrong block.
pain: The business that cannot run without the coach, and the coach does sales, replies and delivery alone.
format: Original: block pulling game with a collapse
story: Pulling out daily jobs makes the tower wobble until it collapses, so the coach sorts jobs into only they can do and the rest, and builds a second tower for the rest.

beats.vo: Your business is a wobbly tower. Guess which block is you.
beats.hero_visual: Full height tower of blocks each labelled with a job: Replies, Reminders, Follow ups, Scheduling, Sales calls, Coaching. The bottom block reads YOU.
beats.motion: Tower sways with a spring, a block slides half out.
beats.sound: Hook hit, wood creak.

beats.vo: Replies. Reminders. Follow ups. Scheduling. All pulled from the same tower. And it all rests on one block.
beats.hero_visual: Close side view as block after block slides out and gets placed on top, tower leaning more with each, until the whole thing tips and crashes across the frame.
beats.motion: Each pull is a fast slide and stack with a growing tilt. Collapse: blocks tumble with squash and bounce, a camera shake of 3 frames.
beats.sound: Wooden slide, stack tap, rumbling crash.

beats.vo: Here is the fix. Write down everything you do in a week. Circle what only you can do. That is the coaching. Everything else is a job for a system.
beats.hero_visual: Blocks lie across the floor. The Coaching block glows violet and floats to the left. Everything else is swept by a line into a second tower on the right.
beats.motion: Violet glow on one block, the rest slide by a sweeping wipe and snap into a neat second tower with a click each.
beats.sound: Soft whoosh, clicks as blocks lock.

beats.vo: Now the tower stands, because you are not holding it up alone. Comment TOWER and I'll DM you the weekly audit sheet.
beats.hero_visual: Two towers side by side, perfectly still, a small sparkle on the top block. Keyword card TOWER.
beats.motion: Towers settle with a 2 percent overshoot. Last frame returns to the first frame wobble for the loop.
beats.sound: Settle thud, pluck.

why_it_stops_scroll: A tower that is about to fall is pure tension. Everyone wants to see the crash, and the sort then snap is the reward.

title: The Receipt
hook_spoken: This is your job description. It is printed on a receipt.
hook_frame0: A thermal receipt printer fills the bottom of the frame with a huge white receipt rolling up out of the top of the screen. Header reads TODAY'S JOB TITLES. Final line, already visible, reads TOTAL: 1 PERSON.
pain: The constant whiplash of wearing opposing hats: coach, marketer, receptionist, tech support, all at once.
format: Original: receipt printer ASMR with a tear off
story: A receipt printer spits out every job a solo coach does, one is circled as the only one that earns, and the rest is torn off onto a second receipt.

beats.vo: This is your job description. It is printed on a receipt.
beats.hero_visual: Giant receipt scrolling up the full frame, TOTAL: 1 PERSON stamped at the bottom.
beats.motion: Receipt feeds upward with a steady ratchet, lines appear row by row.
beats.sound: Hook hit, thermal printer buzz.

beats.vo: Coach. Copywriter. Editor. Receptionist. Scheduler. Collections. Tech support. All of them, at once, by one person.
beats.hero_visual: Close on the text lines racing out of the printer, each job title a huge bold line in black ink on white paper, the paper ripples as it feeds.
beats.motion: Each line prints in with a quick horizontal reveal and a tiny paper jitter. Speed rises, and the last lines stack almost too fast to read.
beats.sound: Print buzz rising in pitch, tick per line.

beats.vo: Only one of those lines is the reason people pay you. Circle it.
beats.hero_visual: A thick violet marker circles the word Coach, ink bleeding slightly, while every other line fades to grey.
beats.motion: Circle draws on with a path stroke and a wobble. Other lines drop to 30 percent with a quick fade.
beats.sound: Marker squeak, soft thud.

beats.vo: Now tear off the rest. Hand each one to a system. We run that part for coaches. Comment HATS and I'll DM you the hat audit.
beats.hero_visual: A serrated tear line sweeps across, the grey lines rip off the strip and flutter into a second receipt headed BACKEND, while the coach's receipt is one clean line. Keyword card HATS.
beats.motion: A tear wipe along a zigzag line, paper piece rotates away, second receipt prints the lines at pace. Keyword card lands.
beats.sound: Paper rip, printer buzz, pluck.

why_it_stops_scroll: A never ending receipt is a known viral shape and the sound is addictive. The ending total is a joke the viewer wants to see land.

title: Find the DM
hook_spoken: Find the DM that is ready to buy. You have ten seconds.
hook_frame0: A screen stuffed with fourteen overlapping app windows, shaking, with a countdown 0:10 in huge numbers across the middle. A tiny violet DM bubble is barely visible under one window. Caption: Find the DM.
pain: Juggling many tools and wrestling with tech stacks, so a real enquiry gets lost in the pile of tabs.
format: Original: find it game then magnetic snap satisfying loop
story: The viewer loses the find it game, then every window snaps into one tidy inbox and the buried DM is answered in a single tap.

beats.vo: Find the DM that is ready to buy. You have ten seconds.
beats.hero_visual: Chaos of windows filling the full frame, countdown 0:10 huge.
beats.motion: Windows jitter and drift, the countdown ticks down fast.
beats.sound: Hook hit, ticking clock.

beats.vo: Too slow. Most coaches keep seven different places where people can message them.
beats.hero_visual: Timer hits zero, a red flash, the bubble slides further under a window. Seven icons without names pop up as big blank tiles, labelled DMs, Email, Form, Texts, Comments, Calendar, Notes.
beats.motion: Timer slams to zero with a shake. Tiles pop in with a stagger.
beats.sound: Buzzer, seven pops.

beats.vo: One inbox. Everything lands in the same place. Watch them snap.
beats.hero_visual: All windows fly toward the center and magnet snap into a neat grid, then fold into one single tall column. Each snap is a tiny flash.
beats.motion: Windows ease in with a magnetic overshoot, grid then column, each one locking with a click flash.
beats.sound: Magnet clicks in a tight cascade, final deep lock.

beats.vo: Now the DM is the first thing you see. Check that one place at set times and nothing hides. Comment MERGE and I'll DM you the one inbox setup.
beats.hero_visual: The column glows and the bubble rises to the top, a violet check draws on, Replied. Keyword card MERGE.
beats.motion: Bubble floats up with an ease, check draws, keyword card lands. The loop returns to the chaos by a quick re scatter.
beats.sound: Pluck, send sound, soft confirm.

why_it_stops_scroll: A visible countdown and a hidden object turn the viewer into a player who feels compelled to search. The snap cascade is a perfect tidy up payoff.

title: The Falling Blocks
hook_spoken: Your week, as a game of falling blocks. There is no spot for the reply.
hook_frame0: A giant falling blocks game board filling the whole screen, stacked to the top with chunky blocks labelled Client call, Client call, Client call. A single violet block labelled Reply hovers above with nowhere to land. Caption: There is no spot for the reply.
pain: Training clients 55 to 60 hours a week leaves zero hours to reply.
format: Original: falling block puzzle, line clear satisfying
story: The reply block cannot fit into a packed week, so a five minute gap is built after each session and the whole row clears.

beats.vo: Your week, as a game of falling blocks. There is no spot for the reply.
beats.hero_visual: Full board, packed, Reply block hovering at the top.
beats.motion: The piece drops one step at a time and bounces off the top of the stack.
beats.sound: Hook hit, arcade blip.

beats.vo: Back to back sessions, all day. Messages come in during the gap that does not exist.
beats.hero_visual: Reply block slams into the pile, the board flashes red, GAME OVER in huge arcade letters, while little DM bubbles pile up behind it.
beats.motion: Slam, red flash, text drops in with a bounce.
beats.sound: Game over jingle (short, not a chime), low thud.

beats.vo: So build the gap. Five minutes after every session, on purpose. It is a block in the week, just like a client.
beats.hero_visual: The board resets. A column of narrow violet blocks labelled Replies, five minutes slides into the gaps between every Client call block.
beats.motion: Blocks fall in turn and lock with a snap, each with a tiny flash.
beats.sound: Lock clicks on a rising scale.

beats.vo: Now watch. Every row clears. Comment BLOCKS and I'll DM you the five minute reply routine.
beats.hero_visual: Rows light up white and clear in a cascade, the whole board collapsing down into a tidy week. Keyword card BLOCKS.
beats.motion: Row flashes, rows vanish with a vertical squash, blocks fall to fill. Keyword card lands.
beats.sound: Line clear whoosh x4, rising pluck.

why_it_stops_scroll: Everybody knows this game and wants to see the piece not fit. The line clear cascade is the most satisfying moment in gaming.

title: Press Rewind
hook_spoken: This call got booked. Rewind to find out why.
hook_frame0: A giant calendar tile reading Booked, Thursday 2pm (Example) with a huge violet rewind symbol over it and a tape counter at 21:00. Caption: Press rewind. Find the message that did it.
pain: Coaches cannot tell which follow up message actually brings someone back (leads die between first message and call, content is not the issue).
format: Original: backwards detective rewind with a single reveal
story: The video rewinds a booked call back through reminders and check ins to one message on day nine that did the work, then breaks down why it worked.

beats.vo: This call got booked. Rewind to find out why.
beats.hero_visual: Calendar tile fills the frame, rewind symbol pulses, counter at 21 days.
beats.motion: Tape counter starts rolling down.
beats.sound: Hook hit, tape whir.

beats.vo: Rewind past the reminders. Rewind past the check ins. Past the first reply.
beats.hero_visual: A flipbook of huge message cards rushes backwards across the screen: Reminder, Reminder, Check in, Check in, First reply, with the day counter ticking down from 21 to 9.
beats.motion: Cards fly in reverse with a motion smear, counter rolls down and slams on 9.
beats.sound: Rewind squeal, tape stop thunk.

beats.vo: Day nine. One message. Is this right for someone like me? They never said it. So the message answered it for them.
beats.hero_visual: A single giant message card centered on black. Four words in big Instrument Serif italic glow: someone like me. Rest of the text types out in plain type.
beats.motion: Card drops into the center with an overshoot, the highlighted words get a violet underline that draws on.
beats.sound: Tape stop thud, typing patter, soft pluck on the phrase.

beats.vo: Write one for your best client type. Name who it is for, then what changed for someone like them. Comment LIKEME and I'll DM you the template.
beats.hero_visual: A fill in the blank template card builds on screen with highlighted gaps. Then the calendar tile flashes back in, Booked. Keyword card LIKEME.
beats.motion: Blanks fill with Example words by a typing reveal, then a whip pan wipe returns to the Booked tile for the loop.
beats.sound: Typing, swish, pluck.

why_it_stops_scroll: A mystery told in reverse makes viewers lean in to find the culprit, and the flipbook rewind is both fun and noisy.

title: The Ice Cube
hook_spoken: This call is booked for next Friday. It will not make it.
hook_frame0: A big ice cube labelled Call, Next Friday sitting on a hot plate, steaming, already dripping. Caption: Will it last until Friday?
pain: Getting people to actually show up after they book is brutal; something came up.
format: Original: melting ice cube metaphor, then a slide to a closer date
story: A call booked far away melts before the day arrives, so the coach moves the booking window closer and the cube stays solid.

beats.vo: This call is booked for next Friday. It will not make it.
beats.hero_visual: Full frame ice cube, labelled Call, Next Friday, melting on a glowing hot plate with steam curling up.
beats.motion: The cube shrinks and drips, puddle spreading.
beats.sound: Hook hit, sizzle and drip.

beats.vo: The further away the date, the more time life has to get in the way. Something came up. Every day is another degree of heat.
beats.hero_visual: A huge week calendar stretches across the frame. The cube slides along it from today to next Friday and shrinks with every day, a thermometer climbing on the side.
beats.motion: Cube slides day by day with a slow melt morph, the thermometer rolls up.
beats.sound: Drips accelerating, sizzle.

beats.vo: Fix it by offering the next two days, not the next two weeks. Show two slots, soon.
beats.hero_visual: The calendar sweeps, only tomorrow and the day after remain lit. A fresh cube is dropped on tomorrow and sits there solid with frost on it.
beats.motion: Wipe cuts away all days except two. Cube lands with a bounce and a frost glow.
beats.sound: Whoosh, ice clink, soft pluck.

beats.vo: Closer date, colder cube. Comment SOON and I'll DM you the booking message we use.
beats.hero_visual: Close on the frosty cube on tomorrow's date, the call card flashes Joined, a breath of cold mist. Keyword card SOON.
beats.motion: Frost grows in a wipe across the cube, the card flips to Joined. Last frame resets with the hot plate for the loop.
beats.sound: Ice crackle, join sound, pluck.

why_it_stops_scroll: A melting cube creates instant suspense and an ASMR drip. Seeing a tiny object under threat makes people watch to the end.

title: Peg Board Drop
hook_spoken: This person wants coaching. Where does the ball land?
hook_frame0: A giant peg board with a violet ball labelled Wants coaching hovering at the top and three buckets at the bottom: Can't afford it, Not this year, Ready. Caption: Where does it land?
pain: They literally do not want to pay; time wasters on discovery calls.
format: Original: peg board drop game with a before and after
story: A ball with no filter lands in the wrong bucket after a long call, so two pegs are added before the booking: price range and timing, and the balls land in the right place.

beats.vo: This person wants coaching. Where does the ball land?
beats.hero_visual: Full height peg board, ball hovering, three labelled buckets.
beats.motion: Ball drops and bounces down through the pegs.
beats.sound: Hook hit, bouncing pings.

beats.vo: Forty minutes on a call. And they cannot afford it.
beats.hero_visual: Ball lands in Can't afford it. A huge timer reads 40:00 wasted in red and a sad stack of empty calendar slots crumbles.
beats.motion: Ball thunks in, timer rolls to 40:00 with a hard stop, slots crumble in pieces.
beats.sound: Dull thud, tick roll, rubble.

beats.vo: Before the call, ask two things in the DM. What range are you thinking of? And how soon do you want to start?
beats.hero_visual: Two new giant pegs snap into the board's top rows, labelled Range and Timing, each with a message bubble that pops from the peg.
beats.motion: Pegs slide in with snaps, bubbles scale up with a back ease.
beats.sound: Two snaps, typing patter.

beats.vo: Now the right ones land where they should. Comment PEGS and I'll DM you the two questions word for word.
beats.hero_visual: Three balls drop one after another, each steered by the pegs into the correct bucket, the Ready bucket flashes Booked (Example). Keyword card PEGS.
beats.motion: Balls bounce with different paths into different buckets, the Ready bucket gets a light sweep. Keyword card lands.
beats.sound: Bouncing pings, bucket clunks, rising pluck.

why_it_stops_scroll: The viewer wants to see where a bouncing ball lands. Changing the board mid video makes the game feel rigged in the best way.

title: Tell Me You're Fully Booked
hook_spoken: Tell me you're fully booked and still panicking, without telling me.
hook_frame0: A full bleed calendar month, every cell packed with solid violet blocks. The next month's page peeks from behind it, totally white, with one red text cursor blinking in the first cell.
pain: Fully booked with delivery but quietly worried about next month, because nobody is replying to the people who asked.
format: Tell me you X without telling me
story: The 'tells' of a fully booked coach who is secretly running dry, ending in a five name check you can do tonight.

beats.vo: Tell me you're fully booked and still panicking, without telling me.
beats.hero_visual: Full bleed packed calendar, violet blocks, the empty white next month behind it with a blinking red cursor.
beats.motion: Cells are already filled at frame 0. A single ripple of brightness crosses the grid, then the page corner peels to expose the blank month.
beats.sound: hookhit at 0, a dry paper peel, one low heartbeat thump.

beats.vo: You refresh your inbox at eleven p.m. to see if anyone new showed up.
beats.hero_visual: A gigantic digital clock reading 11:00 PM fills the screen, each digit the height of the frame, with a tiny glowing inbox icon under it.
beats.motion: Digits roll like a slot reel to 11:00 and land with a 3 percent pop. The inbox icon pulses once, then the red badge reads 0.
beats.sound: Tick roll, soft thud on landing, one tap on the badge.

beats.vo: You scroll the past month and count the names that asked, then went quiet. Seven. Eight. Nine.
beats.hero_visual: A huge vertical list of first names in 200 point type scrolling past (Example names), each one with a small grey 'asked' tag. A running tally in the corner.
beats.motion: Names scroll with ease none then decelerate to a stop on the ninth. The tally rolls up in step with the spoken count.
beats.sound: Swish loop under the scroll, one pluck per count.

beats.vo: Here's tonight's fix. Pick five names from the last thirty days. Send each one line: still on your mind?
beats.hero_visual: Five giant name tags lift off the list one at a time, each turns into a violet message bubble reading 'Still on your mind?' and flies off to the right edge.
beats.motion: Tags peel up with back.out, morph into bubbles, and exit on a straight path to the right with a slight stagger. The blank white next month behind them fills with one violet block per sent message.
beats.sound: Pluck ladder rising C4 to G4, a send whoosh each time.

beats.vo: Comment NEXT and I'll DM you the exact one line messages we use for this.
beats.hero_visual: The next month calendar now half filled, with the keyword 'NEXT' in giant type across it.
beats.motion: Calendar blocks settle, keyword card slams in from the bottom, last frame matches the first frame composition (packed calendar).
beats.sound: Soft pad open, hit on the keyword.

why_it_stops_scroll: A wall of packed calendar with a blank page and a blinking cursor underneath tells a coach 'this is a secret I haven't said out loud' before any word is heard.

title: The Silence Tier List
hook_spoken: I ranked every message coaches send to someone who went quiet.
hook_frame0: A giant S to F tier board with colored rows. A single bubble reading 'Just checking in!' hangs mid air above the F row, trembling, about to drop.
pain: Leads who enquire and then go quiet, and coaches sending weak follow ups.
format: Tier list (S to F rating)
story: Four common follow ups get dropped into tiers, and the S tier turns out to be one simple move a coach can send tomorrow.

beats.vo: I ranked every follow up coaches send to someone who went quiet. Watch where this one lands.
beats.hero_visual: Full screen tier board, rows S A B C D F, bright row colors. 'Just checking in!' bubble trembling above the F row.
beats.motion: Bubble shakes, then drops with a heavy squash into the F row, whole board shakes 2px for 3 frames.
beats.sound: hookhit, then a cartoon low thud, a soft record scratch.

beats.vo: Just checking in. F. It takes their time and gives them nothing. 'Did you see my last message?' D. Now they feel chased.
beats.hero_visual: Close up on the D row. A second bubble slaps in, a red eye icon on it, and a small flushed face bubble appears on the receiving side, backing away.
beats.motion: Board pans left to the D row via a mask wipe, bubble slams, receiver bubble slides out the right edge.
beats.sound: Slap, whoosh, small 'uh oh' pluck.

beats.vo: A discount on the offer. C. You taught them to wait for sales. Saw this and thought of you, plus a short answer to their exact question. A.
beats.hero_visual: Hard cut to a giant 'C' letter filling the frame, then flipping on rotationY to 'A' with a violet bubble that has a play button thumbnail inside.
beats.motion: Letter flips with perspective, bubble lands in the A row with a back.out(1.4) and a light sweep across the row.
beats.sound: Discount: low thud. Flip: card slide. A: rising pluck.

beats.vo: S tier? Close the loop. Send: should I close your file, or is this still on your mind? Nobody likes losing a door.
beats.hero_visual: A huge manila folder with a red 'CLOSE?' tab fills the screen and the S row beneath glows gold violet. The folder's lid hovers open.
beats.motion: Folder drops in with weight, lid cracks open, S row gets a long light sweep. The bubble inside the folder types out.
beats.sound: Paper slide, wooden knock, big satisfying lock-in on S.

beats.vo: Comment TIER and I'll DM you the S tier message, word for word.
beats.hero_visual: The completed tier board dimmed except the S row, with the keyword TIER stamped across it.
beats.motion: Rest of the board fades to 30 percent, keyword stamp slams down, last frame loops to the hanging bubble.
beats.sound: Stamp thud, soft pad.

why_it_stops_scroll: A bubble trembling above the F row is a held breath: you have to see where it falls and what it breaks.

title: Minute Twenty Eight
hook_spoken: I'll never understand why we wait until minute twenty eight of a sales call to ask the budget.
hook_frame0: A huge call timer reading 28:41 filling the top half, a calm call tile below it, and a single giant red question mark over the tile where the coach's face would be.
pain: Wasting time on calls with people who cannot or will not pay; wanting time and price handled before the call.
format: I'll never understand
story: A thirty minute call is slow motion replayed to show where the real question lands, then the three line message that moves it before the call.

beats.vo: I'll never understand why we wait until minute twenty eight of a sales call to ask the budget.
beats.hero_visual: Giant 28:41 timer, call tile with a big red question mark, a dollar sign bubble hovering in the corner.
beats.motion: The timer is already running at frame 0, ticking each second with a micro pop. The dollar bubble drifts in and a red ring pulses around it.
beats.sound: hookhit, clock tick bed, one hollow knock.

beats.vo: Twenty eight minutes of rapport. Of dreams. Of your best advice. And then, 'so, what's your budget?'
beats.hero_visual: A horizontal 30 minute bar fills across the screen in slow motion, filled with tiny coach advice bubbles. At the last sliver, a tall red bubble 'budget?' stabs in.
beats.motion: Bar fills with ease none, bubbles ride on top. The red bubble drops in at the end, bar cracks with a jagged line.
beats.sound: Rising riser, glass crack at the end.

beats.vo: Move three questions to before the call. What do you want. How soon. And what range feels workable.
beats.hero_visual: Three huge stacked cards, each filling a third of the screen, labelled WANT, SOON, RANGE. Each one flips from a question to a green check in turn.
beats.motion: Cards slam up from the bottom one by one with mask wipes, each flips on its check with a small overshoot.
beats.sound: Wooden pluck ladder C4 E4 G4, click on each check.

beats.vo: People who answer are ready to talk. People who vanish just saved you thirty minutes.
beats.hero_visual: Split: left a bright calendar with a green call tile, right a ghost bubble dissolving into a clock that reads 30:00 returned to you, sliding back across the screen into a coach's day bar.
beats.motion: Right side bubble dissolves into particles that stream across the divider and refill a 30 minute slot in the day bar.
beats.sound: Soft whoosh, a satisfying fill sound, small pluck.

beats.vo: Comment BUDGET and I'll DM you the three line message we use for this.
beats.hero_visual: The timer from frame 0, now reading 00:00, with the keyword BUDGET beneath it.
beats.motion: Timer rewinds to zero, keyword slams, final frame matches the first (timer large).
beats.sound: Rewind blip, thud.

why_it_stops_scroll: A call timer already sitting at 28:41 with a red question mark tells a coach 'something is about to go wrong' with the sound off.

title: Would You Rather, Coach Edition

pain: Coaching 55 to 60 hours a week with no time to reply; selling alone, availability on demand.
format: Would you rather
story: A lose-lose choice is shown, then the middle door: a two line holding reply you can send in five seconds.

beats.vo: Would you rather ignore your phone mid session, or ignore the person who just asked to work with you?
beats.hero_visual: Two giant button halves, A and B, a thumb hovering between them. Left: a still client tile. Right: a phone vibrating with a red 4.

beats.hero_visual: Choose A: the client tile turns its back (the tile slides left and dims). Choose B: four bubbles each drop a grey 'seen' stamp then slide off the top.
beats.motion: Two fast match cuts, A resolves with a left slide, B with the four-bubble tumble.
beats.sound: Chair scrape, four small drops.

beats.vo: There's a third door. A two line reply you can send in five seconds. Hey, with a client right now. What made you reach out today?
beats.hero_visual: A giant lock screen with a keyboard shortcut popping a saved reply bubble, the whole screen is the bubble text in big type.
beats.motion: Hard cut to a full screen phone, a long press shows a quick reply menu, the bubble writes itself in by words, thumb taps send. A 5 second ring timer finishes.
beats.sound: Keyboard taps, send whoosh, ring tick.

beats.vo: It buys you an hour, and it starts the conversation. They answer. Then you reply between sessions.
beats.hero_visual: A day bar across the screen: coaching blocks in violet, a small gap in the middle where one reply dot sits and glows green. Four little dots below each carry a check.
beats.motion: Day bar draws on, dot lands in the gap with back.out, checks cascade down.
beats.sound: Pluck ladder, soft confirm.

beats.hero_visual: A phone buzzing in the centre with BUZZ keyword on the screen.
beats.motion: Phone vibration stops on the keyword, last frame matches the opening split.
beats.sound: Hit, soft pad.

pain: Training clients 55 to 60 hours a week leaves no time to reply; selling alone.
format: Day in the life
story: A day timeline is walked hour by hour to find three gaps, and the gaps become reply windows instead of dead time.

beats.vo: A day in the life of a coach who trains fifty five hours a week. Find the five minutes.
beats.hero_visual: Massive circular 24 hour clock ring packed with session blocks, one white sliver pulsing at 12:10 PM.

pain: Enquiring and then ghosting; coaches assuming silence means no and giving up after one message.
format: Myth vs fact
story: A stamp flips from MYTH to FACT, proving silence is not a no and giving a close-the-file message.

beats.vo: Myth. Someone who goes quiet has said no.
beats.hero_visual: Giant MYTH stamp hovering above a bubble 'No reply = No', stamp slams down on the word 'Myth'.
beats.motion: Stamp drops with ease in, ink splatter, whole frame shakes 2px for 3 frames.

beats.motion: Message types in word by word, buttons slide in left and right, a thumb taps YES with a ripple.

beats.motion: Folder slides, closes with a squash, reopens, bubble rises with back.out.

title: Things That Just Make Sense: Show Rate

beats.hero_visual: Two giant interlocking puzzle pieces, left BOOKED, right SHOWED UP, floating toward one another in slow motion.
beats.motion: Pieces drift closer, at the last frame they stop an inch apart and tremble, unsnapped.

beats.vo: Question, answer. Plan, schedule. Reminder, call. Click, click, click.

beats.motion: Pieces snap with a flash, keyword lands, last frame loops back to the almost-snapped pieces.
beats.sound: Big click, bright pluck.

why_it_stops_scroll: Two puzzle pieces trembling an inch apart create a pull to see them click, a satisfying-loop tension that holds the thumb.
